title.en: Afghan boxer accused of killing Scottish aid worker back in court
title.zh: 阿富汗拳击手被控杀害苏格兰援助人员，再次出庭受审

summary.en: Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, from Afghanistan, is back in court facing charges of homicide with intent, robbery, and weapons offences in connection with the killing of a Scottish aid worker.
summary.zh: 26岁的阿富汗拳击手沙里夫·艾哈迈德扎伊因涉嫌杀害一名苏格兰援助人员，面临故意杀人、抢劫和武器犯罪的指控，目前已再次出庭受审。

body.en:
An Afghan boxer suspected of killing a Scottish woman in Greece has arrived in court in Athens for a second time.

Sharif Ahmadzai, who is 26 and from Afghanistan, faces charges of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences.

He is accused of killing aid worker Elisabeth Ross, 38, who was discovered by a homeless man in a derelict building in the Kypseli area of the Greek capital on July 18.

Ahmadzai arrived back in court in Athens on Thursday morning in an unmarked Grey car. He was not pictured. It is expected he will be formally charged later.

On Wednesday, he was assigned a court-appointed lawyer and given time to prepare his defence.

Ahmadzai was initially detained on illegal weapons possession charges and is facing a charge of homicide with intent, as well as allegations that he stole more than €10,000 (£8,500) from the victim's bank accounts using her bank cards.

A statement from the police's organised crime directorate said Ahmadzai was brought to a police station on 30 July "and confessed to his actions".

"In particular, it emerged that the 26-year-old placed the body in a suitcase and transported it to the abandoned site," the statement added.

After allegedly killing Ross, Ahmadzai is accused of sending a series of messages from her phone to her friends and family before switching off the device.

Greek newspapers Proto Thema and Ta Nea have reported that he bought a phone and texted Ross's friends in Athens, impersonating an unnamed jihadist saying he had killed the Scot because of her religion.

The newspapers reported his wife, a US citizen named Alaina Hall, told the police she suspected her husband's involvement in the killing when she woke up to find he was not in their apartment and tracked his phone to where Ross was staying.

Police said Ross - who is from Edinburgh and is known to family and friends as Lisa - had been volunteering with a refugee support group based in Athens.

She arrived in Greece on 26 June and stayed in the Keratsini area of Piraeus until 10 July.

After the body was found, Greek officials contacted Interpol and American authorities were able to identify the fingerprints.
body.zh: 一名涉嫌在希腊杀害一名苏格兰妇女的阿富汗拳击手第二次抵达雅典法庭。 26 岁的谢里夫·艾哈迈德扎伊 (Sharif Ahmadzai) 来自阿富汗，面临故意杀人罪、抢劫罪和武器罪指控。 他被指控杀害了 38 岁的援助人员伊丽莎白·罗斯 (Elisabeth Ross)，一名无家可归者于 7 月 18 日在希腊首都基普塞利地区的一栋废弃建筑中发现了她。 艾哈迈德扎伊周四早上乘坐一辆没有标记的灰色汽车返回雅典法庭。没有拍到他的照片。预计他稍后将被正式指控。 周三，他被指派了一名法庭指定的律师，并有时间准备辩护。 艾哈迈德扎伊最初因非法持有武器罪被拘留，目前面临故意杀人罪的指控，并被指控使用受害者的银行卡从她的银行账户中窃取了超过 10,000 欧元（8,500 英镑）。 警方打击有组织犯罪管理局的一份声明称，艾哈迈德扎伊于 7 月 30 日被带到警察局，“并对自己的行为供认不讳”。 声明补充说：“特别是，这名 26 岁的男子将尸体放入手提箱中，并将其运至废弃地点。” 在涉嫌杀害罗斯后，艾哈迈德扎伊被指控在关闭设备之前用手机向朋友和家人发送了一系列信息。 希腊报纸《Proto Thema》和《Ta Nea》报道说，他买了一部手机，冒充一名未透露姓名的圣战分子给罗斯在雅典的朋友发短信，称他因为苏格兰人的宗教信仰而杀害了她。 据报纸报道，他的妻子，一位名叫阿莱娜·霍尔的美国公民，告诉警方，当她醒来发现丈夫不在他们的公寓里时，她怀疑丈夫参与了这起谋杀案，并通过他的手机追踪到了罗斯住的地方。 警方称，罗斯来自爱丁堡，家人和朋友都称她为丽莎，她一直在雅典的一个难民支持小组做志愿者。 她于6月26日抵达希腊，并在比雷埃夫斯的Keratsini地区停留至7月10日。 尸体被发现后，希腊官员联系了国际刑警组织，美国当局也确认了指纹。

reflection.en: The news of an aid worker's death and the subsequent legal proceedings remind us of the profound human need for justice and accountability. Yahweh calls those in authority to act justly, protect the vulnerable, and ensure that innocent blood is not shed without consequence. As the legal process unfolds, we pray for truth to emerge and for a just resolution...

verse.textZh: 你们要施行公平和公义，拯救被抢夺的脱离欺压人的手。

title.en: Indian journalist Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years in jail for rape
title.zh: 印度记者塔伦·特杰帕尔在2013年强奸案中被定罪

summary.en: The Goa bench of the Bombay High Court has overturned a 2021 trial court verdict, convicting Indian journalist Tarun Tejpal in a 2013 rape case.
summary.zh: 孟买高等法院果阿分院推翻了2021年审判法院的裁决，判定印度记者塔伦·特杰帕尔在2013年强奸案中罪名成立。

body.en:
An Indian court has sentenced former Tehelka magazine editor Tarun Tejpal to 10 years in prison for raping a former colleague, overturning his 2021 acquittal in a decade-old case.

The Goa bench of the Bombay High Court convicted Tejpal under sections of Indian law pertaining to rape and sexual harassment.

Along with jail terms which run concurrently, the court has also ordered him to pay fines adding up to more than 1mn rupees ($10,500; £7,800).

Tejpal, who has denied the accusations, said before the sentencing that he would file an appeal in the Supreme Court.

The allegations against Tejpal, one of India's best-known editors, had made national headlines in 2013. A year before that, thousands of Indians had participated in protests after a brutal gang rape and murder of a woman in Delhi, leading to a larger conversation on sexual violence.

Tejpal's accuser, who cannot be identified under Indian law, said that he sexually assaulted her in a lift during Tehelka's high-profile international conference in Goa in November 2013, an event attended by, among others, Hollywood star Robert De Niro.

Tejpal initially blamed the assault on "a lapse of judgement" and "a misreading of the situation" which had "led to an unfortunate incident that rails against all we believe in and fight for".

But as the case escalated, he issued a statement urging authorities to examine the CCTV footage "so the accurate version of events stands clearly revealed". He also alleged that the case against him was part of a "political vendetta" by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Goa.

Tehelka, the magazine Tejpal co-founded in 2000, had published a number of scoops, many of them based on sting operations.

Some of these stories - including Operation West End in which some of its journalists posed as arms dealers, secretly filming senior army officials, bureaucrats and even the president of the then ruling BJP taking bribes to push through a fake deal - created national and international ripples.

Tejpal was arrested in 2013 and spent seven months in jail until the Supreme Court granted him bail.

In 2021, a sessions court in Goa threw out all the charges against him. But the judge's observations in the 527-page order sparked criticism after she questioned the behaviour of the survivor. .

In photographs taken shortly after the assault, the judge wrote, the young woman was "smiling and looked happy, normal, in [a] good mood".

"She did not look disturbed, reserved, terrified or traumatised in any way even though this was immediately after she claims to have been sexually assaulted," the order said.

Appearing for the Goa government, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta had urged the high court to impose the maximum sentence on Tejpal.

title.en: Who is Abdul El-Sayed? The Michigan doctor who wants to lead the left to the US Senate
title.zh: 阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德是谁？这位密歇根医生希望带领左翼进入美国参议院

summary.en: Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan doctor, has emerged as a prominent progressive figure within the Democratic Party, aiming for a seat in the US Senate.
summary.zh: 密歇根州医生阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德已成为民主党内一位杰出的进步派人物，目标是竞选美国参议员席位。

body.en:
The left-wing Democratic candidate poised to contest a pivotal United States Senate seat in November's midterm elections is a charismatic 41-year-old who once remarked that, if not for an "accident of history", he would likely have been a cab driver in Egypt.

On Wednesday, Abdul El-Sayed secured the Democratic Party's nomination for Michigan's US Senate seat, defeating centrist rival Haley Stevens, who had the backing of the party's leadership.

The former local public health official, known for his charismatic style, is also aiming for a broader role: becoming a leading progressive voice in Washington, opposing President Donald Trump.

Born in Detroit to an Egyptian father and an American mother, he has rapidly emerged as one of the Democratic Party's most prominent progressive figures.

"But for an accident of history that allows my dad to immigrate to Detroit to go to Wayne State University, I was supposed to be a cab driver in Egypt, like my cousins," he said after his narrow primary election victory.

"I got to go to amazing public schools, an incredible public university. I got my medical education paid for," he added. "That's what America gave me."

He is a graduate of the University of Michigan and Columbia University in New York, and he also studied at the University of Oxford in the United Kingdom on the highly regarded Rhodes Scholarship.

He subsequently became the director of public health services for Wayne County, which includes Detroit.

Muscle-bound and an eloquent speaker, El-Sayed proved a deft operator in a primary campaign that was a window into the war within the Democratic Party between the moderate establishment and those further left, like veteran Senator Bernie Sanders.

The 84-year-old Independent helped campaign for El-Sayed and 31-year-old New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

In November, El-Sayed faces a tough battle to beat the Republican nominee, Mike Rogers, a former congressman who has Trump's endorsement.

While both Michigan senators are currently Democrats, it is seen as a swing state. Trump won the traditionally blue-collar, auto-manufacturing state in the 2024 presidential election.

To win, El-Sayed is counting on mobilising a progressive base, outraged by Trump's second term, and on targeting bread-and-butter issues that cut across the political divide.

El-Sayed, who supports universal health care, declared his intention "to get money out of politics, put money in your pocket, pass Medicare for all".

Faced with this left-wing platform, Republicans have labelled him a dangerous extremist, while emphasising his Arab and Muslim identity.

title.en: Iranian footballers who defied Tehran become Australian citizens
title.zh: 反抗德黑兰的伊朗足球运动员成为澳大利亚公民

summary.en: There were among seven to be granted humanitarian visas while playing in Australia - but the other five changed their minds and returned to Iran.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Two Iranian female footballers who publicly defied their government have become Australian citizens.

Atefeh Ramezanisadeh, 34, and Fatemeh Pasandideh, 22, were naturalised in Brisbane, Queensland, on Wednesday.

Ramezanisadeh said it was a "truly special and unforgettable day", while her teammate said "this moment means more than words can express".

They were among seven members of Iran's national team to be granted humanitarian visas while in Australia for the Women's Asian Cup in March - but the other five changed their minds and returned home.

It was feared the team would face repercussions for refusing to sing the Iranian anthem at their opening match, just days after the US-Israeli war against Iran began.

Under pressure from the Iranian community in Australia, authorities initially gave the players a chance to seek asylum – in the end though, only Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh took up the offer.

There was never any question about whether both would become citizens, but the decision comes as the Australian government prepares to introduce tougher visa rules aimed at cutting migration.

The new rules are expected to include restricting the work and appeal rights of asylum seekers and a ban on visitors applying for family visas.

The Australian government has come under increasing pressure from political opponents that promise stricter migration policy, while refugee groups have criticised Australia's current measures, saying they put the safety of asylum seekers at risk.

Ramezanisadeh and Pasandideh were given their citizenship certificates at a ceremony attended by Australian Interior Minister Tony Burke.

Ramezanisadeh recalled "all the challenges we faced" and added that she felt "proud and deeply grateful to become an Australian citizen."

The two players have since been training with A-League Women's team Brisbane Roar, planning to continue their elite sporting careers in Australia.

The drama around the Iranian team unfolded against the background of the war back in their home country which began on 28 February, when Israel and the US launched joint air strikes.

Concerns grew about the team's safety after footage emerged of a host on state TV calling them "traitors" who ought to be punished for their silence during the Iranian anthem on 2 March.

Human rights activists have said the women who returned to Iran may have been pressured to reverse their decisions through threats against their families.

Iran's sports ministry said at the time that the returnees had "defeated the enemy's plans" against them through their "national spirit and patriotism".
body.zh: 两名公开反抗政府的伊朗女足球运动员已成为澳大利亚公民。 34 岁的 Atefeh Ramezanisadeh 和 22 岁的 Fatemeh Pasandideh 于周三在昆士兰州布里斯班入籍。 拉梅扎尼萨德表示，这是“真正特别且难忘的一天”，而她的队友则表示“这一刻的意义超出了言语所能表达的”。 她们是三月份在澳大利亚参加女子亚洲杯期间获得人道主义签证的伊朗国家队七名成员之一，但其他五人改变了主意并回国。 人们担心该队将因拒绝在首场比赛中唱伊朗国歌而面临惩罚，而就在美以对伊朗的战争开始几天后。 在澳大利亚伊朗社区的压力下，当局最初给了球员寻求庇护的机会，但最终只有拉梅扎尼萨德和帕桑迪德接受了这一提议。 对于两人是否会成为公民从来没有任何疑问，但这一决定是在澳大利亚政府准备推出旨在减少移民的更严格的签证规则之际做出的。 预计新规定将包括限制寻求庇护者的工作和上诉权利，以及禁止访客申请家庭签证。 澳大利亚政府面临着来自政治对手的越来越大的压力，他们承诺实施更严格的移民政策，而难民团体则批评澳大利亚目前的措施，称这些措施将寻求庇护者的安全置于危险之中。 拉梅扎尼萨德和帕桑迪德在澳大利亚内政部长托尼·伯克出席的仪式上获得了公民证书。 拉梅扎尼萨德回忆了“我们面临的所有挑战”，并补充说，她“为成为澳大利亚公民而感到自豪和深深的感激”。 此后，这两名球员一直在澳超女子球队布里斯班狮吼队训练，并计划在澳大利亚继续他们的精英体育生涯。 围绕伊朗队的戏剧性事件是在其祖国2月28日开始的战争背景下展开的，当时以色列和美国发动了联合空袭。 3 月 2 日，国家电视台的一名主持人称他们为“叛徒”，他们应该因在伊朗国歌期间保持沉默而受到惩罚，随后视频出现，人们对球队的安全越来越担忧。 人权活动人士表示，返回伊朗的妇女可能因家人受到威胁而被迫改变决定。 伊朗体育部当时表示，返回者通过“民族精神和爱国主义”“击败了敌人针对他们的计划”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to compassion for vulnerable people. Galatians 6:2 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with practical compassion and welcome, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到对脆弱群体的怜悯。Galatians 6:2提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以具体的怜悯与接纳来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.
verse.textZh: 我实在告诉你们，这些事你们既做在我这弟兄中一个最小的身上，就是做在我身上了。

title.en: Air India's new CEO faces financial and safety turbulence
title.zh: 印度航空新任首席执行官面临财务和安全动荡

summary.en: The aftermath of last's year deadly crash and mounting financial losses will be Gebremariam's main challenges.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Air India has appointed a new chief executive as the airline grapples with mounting challenges, including heavy financial losses and the fallout from last year's crash that killed 260 people.

Tewolde Gebremariam succeeds Campbell Wilson, who stepped down from the role in April .

Gebremariam was earlier CEO at Ethiopian Airlines, where he worked for over a decade, growing the regional carrier into one of Africa's largest airlines.

Air India, which Tata Group bought from the Indian government in 2022, has been dealing with a period of operational turbulence.

The airline operates a fleet of 198 aircraft, flying nearly 5,000 weekly flights to 91 destinations in India and abroad, according to the Air India website.

Air India said Gebremariam was unanimously chosen by its board after an extensive search, citing his leadership and operational expertise to steer the airline's "next phase of growth".

N Chandrasekaran, Air India chairman, said: "Having completed the initial phase of stabilisation, integration, and fleet commitments under Campbell's guidance, Air India is now entering a critical execution and expansion era."

Wilson, a former Singapore Airlines executive hired after Tata Group bought Air India nearly four years ago, had signalled in 2024 that he planned to step down in 2026 and had been preparing the airline for a smooth transition.

Now, his replacement Gebremariam has said that he is looking forward to building a "world-class global airline" that "reflects India's extraordinary economic potential".

During his tenure at Ethiopian Airlines, Gebremariam was credited with expanding the fleet nearly threefold and growing it into Africa's most profitable airline.

At Air India, however, Gebremariam faces a daunting task. He takes over as the airline grapples with a series of safety and operational challenges, led by last June's fatal Ahmedabad-London crash, a major setback to its ambitions. The final crash report is due in October.

The airline has continued to struggle since returning to private ownership, reporting a record loss of nearly $2.3bn (£1.7bn) last month. Chandrasekaran has warned a turnaround could take up to a decade. The airline has also cut nearly a third of its international operations.

The airline has also made headlines for a string of operational setbacks. In March, a Delhi-Vancouver flight turned back after nearly eight hours because it lacked clearance to enter Canadian airspace.

These troubles come as India's wider aviation sector faces pressure from rising costs, disrupted international routes due to the Iran war, aircraft delivery delays and tighter regulatory scrutiny.

title.en: You won't believe what we've left in space. It could be nearing a 'tipping point'
title.zh: 你不会相信我们在太空中留下了什么。它可能接近“临界点”

summary.en: Humans have left an extraordinary amount of stuff beyond Earth. What does the SpaceX moon crash tell us about what's to come?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Experts fear space is becoming dangerously crowded, as a new era of exploration sends ever more objects into orbit and to the moon.

The recent crash of a huge chunk of SpaceX rocket debris into the moon has renewed attention on the surprisingly large collection of human-made material in space.

From golf balls, bags of excrement and flags on the lunar surface to rocket wreckage, abandoned tools and countless pieces of debris orbiting Earth, astronomers warn that there are consequences to treating space as a dumping ground.

The bus-sized 4000kg hunk of SpaceX debris came from a Falcon 9 rocket that launched a US and a Japanese lunar lander toward the moon in January last year.

Although no direct image of the impact has emerged, astronomers detected a plume of debris consistent with the rocket crashing into the lunar surface.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Just months ago, four NASA astronauts flew to the moon and back for the first time in more than 50 years. With the second race to the moon well underway — and the United States aiming to establish a base on the lunar surface — the recent SpaceX impact has renewed questions about whether humans are repeating old mistakes off-planet.

Experts say the number of objects orbiting Earth, meanwhile, is increasing the risk of collisions — and without intervention, could make some orbits too dangerous to use.

It's estimated the lunar surface now holds nearly 200 tonnes of human-made material across about 3,000 objects accumulated since the Soviet Union's Luna 2 became the first spacecraft to reach the Moon in 1959.

According to a NASA catalogue, items on the moon include everything from a gold olive branch left behind by Neil Armstrong in 1969, to earplugs, urine collection devices, a hammer, moon boots, cameras, a javelin and two golf balls.

"There are fairly small things all over the moon," associate professor Ben Montet, an astronomy researcher at the University of New South Wales, told SBS News.

"Remnants of the Apollo missions are still there. The lunar lander is there, and the rovers that came with the later missions, but also the silly things like the golf ball that the astronaut on the last mission hit. That's still out there somewhere."

Materials from other moon missions, including robotic probes landed by the former Soviet Union and other nations, also remain scattered across the surface.

Scientists were not particularly concerned about the recent SpaceX collision with the moon's surface, and a NASA spokesperson said it posed no danger to Earth.

Some saw it as an exciting moment that could create an opportunity to study, through telescopes, the lunar material...

title.en: Outrage as Ugandan football captain beaten to death in street gang attack
title.zh: 乌干达足球队长街头遇害引发众怒

summary.en: Police report that Uganda's 27-year-old national football captain was beaten to death by suspected robbers in a street attack after he resisted an attempt to steal his belongings.
summary.zh: 警方称，乌干达27岁的国家足球队队长在街头遭遇抢劫，因反抗盗窃而遭到疑似抢劫犯的殴打致死。

body.en:
Ugandans are mourning the death at 27 of one of the country's best-known footballers after he was beaten by suspected robbers near his home in the capital, Kampala.

Police said David Owori was fatally assaulted after resisting an attempt to steal his mobile phone and other belongings, prompting an outpouring of grief and renewed public anger over violent crime in Uganda.

Owori captained Sports Club (SC) Villa, the Uganda Premier League record champions, where he played both as a right-back and midfielder. He also represented the country's national team - the Cranes.

"We have lost more than a player - we have lost a leader, brother and friend," SC Villa said in a statement.

Witnesses said a group of attackers hit the footballer with paving stones on Tuesday night before robbing Owori of his belongings and fleeing, leaving him unconscious.

SC Villa spokesperson Asan Kasingye told journalists that Owori was targeted just outside his home in Makindye, a Kampala suburb.

"The player was ambushed by thugs as he approached his home, leaving him with life-threatening injuries before he was rushed to the medical facility," Kasingye said.

Owori was rushed to a nearby medical clinic and then transferred to a private facility in the city, but he died of his injuries on Wednesday.

Local police spokesperson Rachael Kawala said detectives were pursuing leads to identify those responsible.

"The scene of the incident has been documented and processed to ensure that all relevant evidence is collected and preserved," Kawala added.

Owori's murder has sent shockwaves across Uganda, with the football community, including fans and teammates, and politicians demanding justice.

Tributes are continuing to pour in for the defender, who was popularly known as Colgate.

The Federation of Uganda Football Associations (Fufa) described Owori as "a true leader on and off the pitch".

"David was not just a footballer. He was both a leader and an inspiration to a generation," it said in a statement.

The national side, the Cranes, said the team had lost a football star who "carried the hopes" of Uganda.

Parliament on Wednesday observed a minute's silence in honour of Owori and called for a quick investigation.

The versatile player, renowned for his tactical discipline and ability to feature across midfield, returned to SC Villa in 2023 - after two years in Europe - for a second spell. At the time of his death, he was among the longest-serving members of the current squad.

He helped lead the high-profile team to their first league title in 20 years securing a record 17th top-flight crown in 2024.

His influence on and off the pitch earned him a contract extension until January 2027 with the team.

title.en: What's behind the Algeria-Morocco rivalry?
title.zh: 阿尔及利亚与摩洛哥宿怨的背后是什么？

summary.en: Morocco and Algeria have maintained a decades-long rivalry, primarily centered on the territory of Western Sahara, but now encompassing a broader range of issues.
summary.zh: 摩洛哥和阿尔及利亚两国之间的宿怨已持续数十年，主要围绕西撒哈拉领土问题，但如今其竞争已远超该领土范围。

body.en:
Morocco and Algeria have been at odds for decades, chiefly over the territory of Western Sahara. But their rivalry now extends far beyond the territory.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez traveled to Algeria  on July 20 for talks with Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune and Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb.

The meeting's aim was to resolve a diplomatic row that erupted between both countries in 2022 after Spain sided with Morocco's autonomy proposal to resolve the Western Sahara conflict — much to Algeria's dismay.

It is a matter of debate whether Spain's rapprochement with Algeria outraged Morocco  so much that it deliberately allowed tens of thousands of migrants to storm the Spanish exclave of Ceuta , even though both countries have improved their relations enormously in recent years. Spanish daily El Pais has certainly entertained the possibility of Moroccan meddling.

"Ceuta tensions coincided with Pedro Sanchez's trip to Algeria, a regional rival of the [Moroccan] Alawite Kingdom," an  opinion piece in the Spanish paper notes. The article later states that "any attempt to use immigration as a bargaining chip is unacceptable."

Moroccan interior ministry spokesperson Rachid El Khalfi has rejected such accusations, saying the incident resulted from "the malicious exploitation of the digital space," as well as "misleading information" and misinterpretations of a recent Spanish Supreme Court ruling on the rights of arriving migrants.

Experts interviewed by DW say that while potentially deliberate inaction by Moroccan border guards contributed to the breach, it's unlikely the country intended to instigate such a major diplomatic incident .

The recent Ceuta incident and subsequent accusations point to the deep-seated rivalry between Algeria and Morocco. At its heart lies the conflict over Western Sahara, which began when Spain withdrew from the territory in 1975. A conflict between the Polisario Front, which fights for the Sahrawi people's right to self-determination, and Morocco ended in 1991 with a UN-brokered ceasefire. A planned referendum to allow Saharawis to determine its future has never taken place, and the UN considers it Africa's last non-self governing territory.

Morocco, relying on historical claims, considers the region an indispensable part of its own national territory, and has sought international recognition for its integration as a semi-autonomous province. Algeria, in contrast, supports Western Sahara's independence and backs the Polisario Front.The European Court of Justice ruled in 2024 that Morocco and Western Sahara are distinct territories.

The Western Sahara conflict has long since become a symbol of a deeper rivalry between Algeria and Morocco over influence in the Maghreb...
body.zh: 摩洛哥和阿尔及利亚几十年来一直存在分歧，主要是在西撒哈拉领土问题上。但他们的竞争现在已经远远超出了领土范围。 西班牙首相佩德罗·桑切斯于7月20日前往阿尔及利亚，与阿尔及利亚总统阿卜杜勒马吉德·特布恩和总理西菲·格里布举行会谈。 这次会议的目的是解决2022年两国之间爆发的外交争端，此前西班牙支持摩洛哥解决西撒哈拉冲突的自治提案——这让阿尔及利亚非常沮丧。 西班牙与阿尔及利亚的和解是否激怒了摩洛哥，以至于摩洛哥故意允许数万名移民涌入西班牙飞地休达，这是一个有争议的问题，尽管两国近年来关系已经大大改善。西班牙日报《国家报》无疑考虑到了摩洛哥干预的可能性。 “休达的紧张局势恰逢佩德罗·桑切斯访问阿尔及利亚，阿尔及利亚是[摩洛哥]阿拉维派王国的地区竞争对手，”西班牙报纸上的一篇评论文章指出。文章随后指出，“任何利用移民作为讨价还价筹码的企图都是不可接受的”。 摩洛哥内政部发言人拉希德·埃尔·哈尔菲否认了此类指控，称该事件是“对数字空间的恶意利用”以及“误导性信息”和对西班牙最高法院最近关于抵达移民权利的裁决的误解造成的。 接受德国之声采访的专家表示，虽然摩洛哥边防部队可能故意不采取行动，导致了这次违规行为，但该国不太可能有意煽动如此重大的外交事件。 最近的休达事件和随后的指控表明阿尔及利亚和摩洛哥之间根深蒂固的竞争。其核心是西撒哈拉冲突，这场冲突始于 1975 年西班牙从该领土撤军。争取撒哈拉人民自决权的波利萨里奥阵线与摩洛哥之间的冲突于 1991 年以联合国斡旋的停火结束。计划中的让撒哈拉人决定其未来的全民投票从未举行过，联合国认为它是非洲最后一个非自治领土。 摩洛哥依据历史主张，认为该地区是其国家领土不可或缺的一部分，并寻求国际承认其作为半自治省的一体化。相比之下，阿尔及利亚支持西撒哈拉独立并支持波利萨里奥阵线。欧洲法院于2024年裁定摩洛哥和西撒哈拉是不同的领土。 西撒哈拉冲突早已成为阿尔及利亚和摩洛哥之间争夺马格里布影响力的更深层次竞争的象征……

title.en: Hiroshima survivors warn against Japan's rearmament
title.zh: 广岛幸存者警告日本重新武装的风险

summary.en: On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists expressed concern to DW that Japan's military buildup risks undermining its long-held commitment to pacifism.
summary.zh: 在原子弹爆炸周年纪念日之际，幸存者和活动家向德国之声表示，日本的军事建设可能削弱其长期以来对和平主义的承诺。

body.en:
On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.

Japan on Thursday commemorates the 81st anniversary of the nuclear attack on  Hiroshima .

On August 6, 1945, the US dropped an atomic bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima during the last days of World War II , killing close to 80,000 people in the initial blast. Three days later, the US dropped a bomb over Nagasaki.

"Japan adopted a pacifist constitution in reflection on World War II," noted Masako Wada, assistant secretary general of  Nihon Hidankyo , or the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers' Organizations. 

Japan "earned the trust of the international community as a country that promised never to wage a war again," added Wada, who survived the Nagasaki bombing as a 1-year-old.

However, in recent years, Japan has increased defense spending, eased restrictions on weapons exports and expanded the role of its military, citing growing risks from China , North Korea and Russia .

"The current administration is destroying that [trust]," Wada told DW, referring to Japan's recent efforts to pivot away from decades of strict postwar pacifism.

"Japan's recent military buildup is no different from recreating the arms race that led the country toward World War II," said 84-year-old Masashi Ieshima, who survived the Hiroshima bombing at the age of 3.

Ieshima was playing in the entrance of his house, just 1.2 miles (2 km) from the hypocenter, when the blast shattered all the windows in the house, sending shards of glass into his mother.

Seventy years later, he underwent surgery for thyroid cancer, which was officially recognized as an atomic bomb-related illness. His father, who was also exposed to the Hiroshima atomic bombing, died of laryngeal cancer.

"It makes my blood boil to see Japan justify its military buildup and the easing of arms export restrictions over the possibility of a Taiwan conflict ," said Ieshima, who serves as the chairman of Toyukai, the Tokyo affiliate of Nihon Hidankyo.

"If Japan continues down this path, it could lead to war. And if another war breaks out, I believe it will be a nuclear war." 

The average age of Japan's atomic bomb survivors, known as "hibakusha," has reached almost 87. They face the urgent challenge of passing on their testimony and calls for peace to younger generations, including their children, grandchildren, and supporters.

Takako Nakamura, a second-generation atomic bomb survivor from Nagasaki, began working actively as a family testimony speaker in February 2026, following her career retirement.

body.zh: 在原子弹爆炸周年纪念日之际，幸存者和活动人士告诉德国之声，日本的军备建设有可能侵蚀其对和平主义的长期承诺。 日本周四纪念广岛核袭击 81 周年。 1945 年 8 月 6 日，美国在第二次世界大战的最后几天向日本广岛投下了一颗原子弹，在最初的爆炸中造成近 8 万人死亡。三天后，美国在长崎投下了一颗炸弹。 日本原子弹受害者组织联合会助理秘书长和田正子指出：“日本通过了一部和平主义宪法，以反思第二次世界大战。” 一岁时在长崎原子弹爆炸中幸存下来的和田补充道，日本“作为一个承诺不再发动战争的国家赢得了国际社会的信任”。 然而，近年来，日本以来自中国、朝鲜和俄罗斯的风险日益增加为由，增加了国防开支，放宽了对武器出口的限制，并扩大了军队的作用。 “现任政府正在摧毁这种[信任]，”和田告诉德国之声，他指的是日本最近努力摆脱几十年来严格的战后和平主义。 “日本最近的军备建设无异于重现导致该国走向第二次世界大战的军备竞赛，”3 岁时在广岛原子弹爆炸中幸存下来的 84 岁老人家岛雅志 (Masashi Ieshima) 说。 伊江岛正在自家门口玩耍，距离震源仅 1.2 英里（2 公里），爆炸震碎了房子里的所有窗户，玻璃碎片飞进了他的母亲体内。 七十年后，他接受了甲状腺癌手术，甲状腺癌被正式认定为与原子弹相关的疾病。他的父亲也曾遭受广岛原子弹爆炸，因喉癌去世。 担任日本飞段协东京分公司东友会董事长的家岛说：“看到日本证明其军事集结和放松武器出口限制是合理的，这让我热血沸腾。” “如果日本继续走这条路，可能会导致战争。如果另一场战争爆发，我相信这将是一场核战争。” 日本原子弹幸存者（被称为“原爆幸存者”）的平均年龄已接近 87 岁。他们面临着向年轻一代，包括他们的子孙和支持者传递他们的证词和和平呼吁的紧迫挑战。 来自长崎的第二代原子弹幸存者中村贵子 (Takako Nakamura) 在职业生涯退休后，于 2026 年 2 月开始积极担任家庭证词发言人。 “人们被杀得无影无踪，连骨头都没有留下。这就是原子弹的真正本质，”...

reflection.en: The survivors' plea against rearmament echoes the ancient prophetic call for nations to turn away from instruments of war. Their lived experience reminds us of the profound human cost of conflict and the enduring hope for a world where weapons are transformed into tools for peace. This vision, where swords become plowshares, invites us to consider how...
reflection.zh: 幸存者反对重新武装的呼吁，与古老的先知呼唤国家放弃战争工具不谋而合。他们的亲身经历提醒我们冲突带来的人类深重代价，以及对一个武器转化为和平工具的世界的持久盼望。这种“化剑为犁”的愿景，邀请我们思考社会如何才能真正建立持久的安全。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: Austria breaks temperature record as heatwave sweeps across Europe
title.zh: 奥地利气温打破纪录，热浪席卷欧洲

summary.en: Europe has experienced extreme heatwaves and wildfires this summer, with Austria breaking temperature records, particularly affecting Mediterranean countries.
summary.zh: 今年夏天，欧洲经历了极端热浪和野火，奥地利气温打破纪录，地中海国家受影响尤为严重。

body.en:
Austria has recorded its highest ever temperature, while Hungarians curbed power use as the latest heatwave and drought took their toll on central and southern Europe.

Europe, the world's fastest-warming continent, has been ravaged by record-breaking heat and destructive wildfires throughout its summer, with France and Spain particularly hard hit in recent weeks.

The focus of the heatwave has shifted further east, with Italy placing its major cities under a red heat alert as temperatures climbed to around 40C in some areas. In Albania, emergency services battled a wildfire in the southern region of Mallakaster.

The heat prompted the Vatican to move Pope Leo's first weekly general audience after the July break indoors rather than hold it in St Peter's Square. Visitors to Rome welcomed the decision as they sought relief from the sweltering conditions.

"I suppose it's better to hold it indoors because of the heat," Diego Amaya, a tourist from Mexico, said.

The temperature hit a record 41.2 C in the Austrian town of Bad Deutsch-Altenburg near the border with Slovakia on Wednesday, national weather service GeoSphere Austria said. The previous record of 41C was set on Tuesday in nearby Vienna.

Across the border in Hungary, companies and households cut power consumption this week after a government appeal to ease pressure on the grid amid the severe drought. The capital Budapest is facing the peak of the heatwave over the next two days, with temperatures rising close to 40C on Wednesday.

Dwindling water levels on the Danube have forced Hungary to largely shut down its sole nuclear plant, which uses the river's waters for cooling, creating an energy crisis that has stretched power supply capacity to its limits.

Slovenia's only nuclear power plant, Krsko, which supplies neighbouring Croatia as well, said on Wednesday it would begin reducing reactor output overnight due to exceptionally high temperatures and low flows on the Sava River, which flows into the Danube. The plant will initially cut generation to 80 per cent of capacity.

Further west, water levels on the river Rhine in Germany have hit new lows, with some cargo services stopping and other sailings continuing but with greatly reduced loads. The Rhine is a route for commodities including grains, ores and petrol.

In Albania's southern Mallakaster region, wildfires forced the evacuation of about 15 families along with their livestock and pets, while ground and aerial crews fought to stop the flames reaching homes near a village.

title.en: School-bus-sized SpaceX rocket chunk crashes into Moon
title.zh: 校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁月球

summary.en: A school-bus-sized chunk of a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon, raising concerns among experts about increasing lunar debris. This incident occurs amidst a growing space race between the United States and China to send humans back to the Moon.
summary.zh: 一块校车大小的SpaceX火箭残骸坠毁在月球上，引发专家对月球垃圾日益增多的担忧。此事发生在中美两国竞相将人类送回月球之际。

body.en:
A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's the latest instance of lunar litter — rubbish left behind on the moon — that some experts believe could become a greater concern as the United States and China race to put astronauts on the moon .

In 2022, a Chinese rocket unintentionally hit the moon following a lunar mission, and more stray rocket pieces could have struck the moon in past decades without scientists' knowledge.

Julianna Scheiman, director of Dragon Human Spaceflight at SpaceX, said the company is working with NASA to avoid future wrecks.

She also emphasised that the projected crash was not deliberate. A combination of solar activity and gravity accidentally put it on a collision course with the moon, according to Scheiman.

Carl Schmidt, a planetary scientist at Boston University, said he is "100 per cent certain" that his team's observations revealed signs of the lunar crash.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

"We don't have images of the impact", but there is telescope evidence, Schmidt said in email correspondence shared with media.

Even before signs of the debris plume were spotted by the telescope in Chile, retired astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell noted that observations of the dead upper stage on Tuesday night showed it heading straight for the moon.

The anticipated crash site was a dusty, barren patch near Einstein Crater on the moon's sunlit western limb — near the edge of the near and far sides, which is especially difficult to observe from Earth.

summary.en: Russia is preparing a new mobilization campaign to boost troop numbers, Ukrainian officials and independent Russian media outlets report. The Kremlin denies this.

According to Zelenskyy, Russian President Vladimir Putin is reportedly preparing to recruit additional Russian soldiers to fight in the war against Ukraine .

"He is concealing his intention behind different words and signals, but he is making preparations," Zelenskyy said. "It is important that we, together with our partners, exert sufficient pressure on Russia so that the idea of ending this aggression — the idea of peace, rather than further Russian mobilization — prevails," he added. The Ukrainian president also said Russia's army was losing more fighters at the front than it can recruit, even though Putin wants to intensify the attacks and expand the war.

Putin issued a decree in autumn 2022 launching a "partial mobilization," which remains in effect to this day, as confirmed by the presidential administration in 2023. The document, it said, "regulates additional measures necessary to ensure that the armed forces fulfill their objectives."

A piece of a SpaceX rocket that has been floating in space for the past year has slammed into the moon, according to scientists.

Although no-one observed the collision, a telescope in Chile spotted what astronomers have identified as a debris plume resulting from the crash.

Space tracking experts said it was inevitable that the leftover rocket segment would plough into the moon .

The school-bus-sized object is the second stage ‌of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket that had launched a lunar lander from Firefly Aerospace toward the moon in January 2025.

Weighing 4,000kg, the rocket piece had been due to hit the moon at around 4.35pm AEST on Wednesday, travelling at around 8,690km/h.

The European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope also detected a stream of sodium and lithium stretching for tens of kilometres into space for at least five to 10 minutes following the impact, Schmidt added.

As weather events become more extreme, fake videos are being shared rapidly online, and it’s causing real world problems in China.

The government has vowed to crack down on misinformation, but as our China correspondent Stephen McDonell explains, identifying AI-generated content is becoming increasingly difficult.
body.zh: 随着天气事件变得更加极端，虚假视频在网上迅速传播，这给中国带来了现实世界的问题。 政府发誓要打击错误信息，但正如我们的中国记者斯蒂芬·麦克唐纳（Stephen McDonell）所解释的那样，识别人工智能生成的内容变得越来越困难。

reflection.en: The rapid spread of fake videos, especially during times of crisis, reminds us how a small piece of misinformation can ignite significant real-world problems. Just as a tiny spark can set a vast forest ablaze, unchecked falsehoods online can cause widespread confusion and harm. This highlights the profound impact of what we share and the need for careful...
reflection.zh: 虚假视频的迅速传播，尤其是在危机时期，提醒我们一小段错误信息如何能引发重大的现实问题。正如一点火星能点燃整片森林，网络上未经核实的虚假信息也能造成广泛的混乱和伤害。这突显了我们所分享内容产生的深远影响，以及在数字时代谨慎辨别的必要性。

verse.textEn: The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.
verse.textZh: 舌头在百体里也是最小的，却能说大话。看哪，最小的火能点着最大的树林。

title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，批评者担心中国可能填补外交真空

summary.en: The US State Department plans to close five foreign consulates and missions across Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia, and Cameroon. This decision has drawn criticism, with concerns that it could create a diplomatic vacuum that other nations, such as China, might seek to fill.
summary.zh: 美国国务院计划关闭在加拿大、格林纳达、日本、印度尼西亚和喀麦隆的五个领事馆和外交使团。这一决定引发了批评，有人担心这可能造成外交真空，并可能被其他国家（如中国）填补。

body.en: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国国务院通知国会计划关闭加拿大、格林纳达、日本、印度尼西亚和喀麦隆 美国国务院将关闭亚洲、非洲、北美和加勒比地区的五个外国领事馆和使团，此举招致批评，称此举留下的外交真空有可能被中国填补。美国国会已收到即将关闭工厂的通知，出于成本考虑，关闭工厂是合理的，并且自唐纳德·特朗普 2025 年 1 月重返白宫以来，美国对美国与一系列国家的双边关系进行了重新评估。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The decision to close diplomatic missions highlights the importance of international engagement and the potential consequences when a presence is withdrawn. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that where there is no guidance, a nation may falter, emphasizing the value of wise counsel and sustained diplomatic presence for global stability. In a complex world, Yahweh's...
reflection.zh: 关闭外交使团的决定凸显了国际参与的重要性，以及撤回存在可能带来的后果。箴言11:14提醒我们，没有引导，国家就会衰落，这强调了明智的忠告和持续的外交存在对全球稳定的价值。在一个复杂的世界中，雅伟的智慧可以引导领袖们做出促进国家间和平与理解的决定。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
title.zh: 当愚蠢的人类押注机器智能时，民主就岌岌可危 | 拉斐尔·贝尔

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence challenges us to consider the limits of human understanding and the wisdom needed to govern powerful new technologies. As we navigate this complex future, Yahweh's word reminds us not to lean solely on our own intellect or creations, but to seek a deeper, divine wisdom. True discernment comes from trusting in...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的迅速发展促使我们思考人类理解的局限性，以及管理强大新兴科技所需的智慧。当我们驾驭这个复杂的未来时，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要单单依靠自己的智力或创造物，而要寻求更深层的、来自雅伟的智慧。真正的洞察力来自于全心信靠雅伟，尤其是在面对影响社会根基的决策时。

verse.textEn: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: A moment that changed me: I found a forbidden novel – it led to a dangerous, lasting love
title.zh: 一个改变我的时刻：我发现了一本禁书——它带来了一段危险而持久的爱

summary.en: A Uyghur woman recounts how finding a forbidden novel in Xinjiang led her to embrace her culture and a lasting love, despite societal disapproval.
summary.zh: 一位维吾尔族女性讲述了她在新疆发现一本禁书后，如何因此拥抱自己的文化并找到一份持久的爱，尽管这在社会上受到非议。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...

reflection.en: This story highlights the courage to follow one's heart and embrace one's identity, even when cultural norms or authorities forbid it. It reminds us that there are times when our deepest convictions, aligned with Yahweh's truth, call us to a path different from what human systems dictate.
reflection.zh: 这个故事彰显了追随内心、拥抱自我身份的勇气，即便文化规范或权威禁止。它提醒我们，有时我们最深刻的信念，与雅伟的真理相符，会召唤我们走一条不同于人类体系所规定的道路。

verse.textZh: 顺从神，不顺从人，是应当的。

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: You won't believe what we've left in space. It could be nearing a 'tipping point'

summary.en: Humans have left an extraordinary amount of stuff beyond Earth. What does the SpaceX moon crash tell us about what's to come?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Experts fear space is becoming dangerously crowded, as a new era of exploration sends ever more objects into orbit and to the moon.

The recent crash of a huge chunk of SpaceX rocket debris into the moon has renewed attention on the surprisingly large collection of human-made material in space.

From golf balls, bags of excrement and flags on the lunar surface to rocket wreckage, abandoned tools and countless pieces of debris orbiting Earth, astronomers warn that there are consequences to treating space as a dumping ground.

The bus-sized 4000kg hunk of SpaceX debris came from a Falcon 9 rocket that launched a US and a Japanese lunar lander toward the moon in January last year.

Although no direct image of the impact has emerged, astronomers detected a plume of debris consistent with the rocket crashing into the lunar surface.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Just months ago, four NASA astronauts flew to the moon and back for the first time in more than 50 years. With the second race to the moon well underway — and the United States aiming to establish a base on the lunar surface — the recent SpaceX impact has renewed questions about whether humans are repeating old mistakes off-planet.

Experts say the number of objects orbiting Earth, meanwhile, is increasing the risk of collisions — and without intervention, could make some orbits too dangerous to use.

It's estimated the lunar surface now holds nearly 200 tonnes of human-made material across about 3,000 objects accumulated since the Soviet Union's Luna 2 became the first spacecraft to reach the Moon in 1959.

According to a NASA catalogue, items on the moon include everything from a gold olive branch left behind by Neil Armstrong in 1969, to earplugs, urine collection devices, a hammer, moon boots, cameras, a javelin and two golf balls.

"There are fairly small things all over the moon," associate professor Ben Montet, an astronomy researcher at the University of New South Wales, told SBS News.

"Remnants of the Apollo missions are still there. The lunar lander is there, and the rovers that came with the later missions, but also the silly things like the golf ball that the astronaut on the last mission hit. That's still out there somewhere."

Materials from other moon missions, including robotic probes landed by the former Soviet Union and other nations, also remain scattered across the surface.

Scientists were not particularly concerned about the recent SpaceX collision with the moon's surface, and a NASA spokesperson said it posed no danger to Earth.

summary.en: New regulations are currently being developed for the sale of electric bikes, scooters, and skateboards across Australia.

body.en:
A nationwide crackdown on high-speed e-bikes will seek to close regulatory loopholes after years of rising accidents and injuries, the federal government has announced.

On Thursday, Labor instructed the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) to draft new standards for the sale of "e-micromobility" devices.

The new standards will apply to electric bikes, scooters and skateboards and are designed to prevent the sale of high-risk devices following a spike in e-bike injuries.

Assistant Competition Minister Andrew Leigh said the changes would inspire confidence in Australian consumers and send a clear message to industry.

"Nationally consistent standards will provide clearer expectations for manufacturers, retailers and consumers alike," he said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Currently, regulatory enforcement varies between states and territories. Retailers can exploit the resultant loopholes to sell non-compliant devices.

Last year, Australia's state transport ministers agreed to mandate the international EN 15194 standard as the primary benchmark for e-bikes.

These standards restrict e-bikes to operating primarily through pedal assistance, cap their output, and require them to cut power once they reach 25km/h.

The new rules drafted by the ACCC will aim to close existing gaps after years of concerns over injuries and accidents, including from high-powered e-bikes.

The new consumer standards were proposed at a meeting of federal, state and territory consumer affairs ministers in Darwin in July.

Harold Scruby, chief executive at the Pedestrian Council of Australia, said the announcement was a welcome step forward, but long overdue.

Any changes must be complemented by consequences for retailers who fail to meet compliance standards, Scruby said.

"We've really got to clamp down on these cowboys who are selling these things to young children," he said.

Asked whether the horse had already bolted, Leigh insisted the changes complemented state-level crackdowns.

"There's work underway through transport ministers," he told Seven's Sunrise program on Thursday.

E-bikes have been spruiked as an environmentally friendly, cost-affordable answer to congested city streets.

But the rollout of shared e-bike schemes — like Lime bikes and others — as well as their broader uptake across the nation have been clouded by rising injury and accident rates.

In 2024, NSW recorded 226 injuries related to e-bikes, which surged to 233 in the first seven months of 2025, including four deaths.

In Queensland, more than 6000 emergency department presentations were linked to e‑mobility devices between 2022 and 2025.

body.en:
Millions of borrowers will be watching closely when the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) announces its latest interest rates decision next week.

A mortgage expert says it will be a close call despite expectations among the 'big four' banks — Commonwealth Bank, Westpac, NAB and ANZ — that the central bank will leave the cash rate on hold at 4.35 per cent.

The RBA has already lifted rates three times this year, while governor Michele Bullock has refused to rule out further hikes as inflation remains above its 2-3 per cent target band.

"They've got a clock ticking in the background, particularly when it comes to inflation," said Sally Tindall, the data insights director at Canstar.

"The RBA board has repeatedly said that time is a factor in this battle with inflation because the longer we take to get back down, the harder it becomes, and the more entrenched inflation becomes".

The board will examine three key economic indicators released in recent weeks before handing down its decision on Tuesday.

Inflationary pressures, as measured by both the consumer price index (CPI) and trimmed mean inflation, are frequently cited in the RBA's statements on its decision-making.

In June, the RBA said inflation was still too high and warned higher fuel and commodity costs are starting to flow into other parts of the economy, including housing and construction.

Bullock said Australia already had an inflation problem before disruptions to global oil markets caused by conflict in the Middle East.

The most recent data from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) showed a shift in inflation in June.

Headline inflation fell from 4 per cent to 3.8 per cent while the trimmed mean, which strips out volatile items, remained steady at 3.6 per cent.

Tindall said that inflation predictions have shifted over time primarily due to the war in the Middle East, which has added to inflationary pressures.

The figures for June were "perhaps better than we were expecting," Tindall said, "but still a long way from target".

The RBA aims to bring inflation down to between 2 and 3 per cent, fulfilling one of its mandates to keep it low and stable.

Its other mandate is to support full employment, meaning as many Australians in work as possible without creating excessive inflation.

In June, the unemployment rate was 4.4 per cent, slightly below the 2026 peak of 4.5 per cent in April.

These figures have been on the RBA governor's mind. Earlier this month, Bullock said they were higher than expected.

title.en: 'Extremely grateful': Labor MP Ed Husic escapes serious injury after car accident
title.zh: “非常感激”：工党议员埃德·胡西克在车祸后幸免于重伤

summary.en: The Chifley MP suffered fractures and a concussion after being rear-ended at 80km/h on a motorway in western Sydney.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An outspoken Labor backbencher has walked away from a car crash on a motorway, avoiding "serious injury".

Chifley MP Ed Husic was driving home from his western Sydney electorate office on Tuesday when he was involved in a serious motor accident.

Paramedics on the scene reported a truck rear-ended Husic's car while travelling at about 80km/h on the M7 motorway.

The Labor MP sustained minor abrasions, fractures and a concussion and was taken to the nearby Westmead Hospital to be assessed.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

In a post on Instagram, he said he was "extremely grateful to walk away from the accident without more serious injury", and will take a short period of leave from parliamentary duties to fully recover.

"Mr Husic thanked the doctors, nurses and paramedics at Westmead Hospital for providing him with outstanding care and thanked his family and friends for their support, especially during his hospital stay," the statement said.

In July, the backbencher used an appearance at Labor's national conference to push for stronger criticism of Israel in the party's platform, but the motion was quashed by factional leaders.

title.en: High Court finds secret recording can be used as evidence in domestic violence case
title.zh: 高庭裁定秘密录音可作为家庭暴力案件证据

summary.en: Recordings of private conversations are usually illegal, and experts say the ruling is a major milestone for survivors.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Victim-survivors of domestic violence might now be able to use secret recordings of admissions of abuse to seek safety after a major High Court decision.

Australia's highest court on Wednesday dismissed an appeal from a man convicted of raping his wife while she slept on two occasions.

He had argued a recording of him admitting to the first rape was obtained illegally.

While most recordings of private conversations are illegal , the High Court found the recording was allowed and able to be used as evidence because it was necessary to protect the victim's "bodily autonomy and integrity".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"The covert recording was the reminder to the complainant, by replaying it to herself, to avoid being exposed to the real risk of being raped," the court said in its unanimous judgment.

"The interest of a person in not being raped is an interest deserving of the very strongest protection."

The man, known by the pseudonym Potter, was found guilty in South Australia of raping his sleeping wife on two occasions while the jury could not reach a verdict on two further counts.

A month before the last rape, his wife recorded a conversation on her phone where she confronted Potter about the attacks, and he admitted to doing them.

The woman gave evidence that she made the recording to "convince myself never to go back to him no matter what happened".

Heather Douglas is a legal expert and professor at Melbourne Law School. She said protecting the rights of victim-survivors to record — and use as evidence — confessions of abuse inflicted on them is a major milestone for domestic violence law in Australia.

"The decision is important as it explicitly recognises that a lawful interest includes a right of bodily autonomy and integrity in the context of recordings," Douglas said.

The influence of the High Court's decision could extend beyond criminal cases, potentially allowing for similar recordings to be used in protection applications, according to Douglas.

However, it remains to be seen how far courts will allow secret recordings to be used to as evidence against less obvious forms of abuse.

Douglas believes, "much of the most damaging domestic and family violence is non-physical, such as coercive control, and this form of abuse impacts autonomy".

summary.en: Will a new policy change push people to drop their private health insurance coverage?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Since the federal government announced earlier this year it would scrap the higher private health insurance rebate for people aged 65 and over, opponents have come out in force.

Private Healthcare Australia, the insurers’ peak body, says the government’s own modelling of about 44,000 older Australians dropping their cover due to the resulting higher premiums is a "significant underestimate”.

Three state health ministers have warned the change would push more people into their strained public hospitals.

So how many people would really drop their cover as a result of this policy change?

Our new research , designed specifically to test this question, gives some clues. In a nutshell, the sky won’t fall in.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Right now, the private health insurance rebate depends on both income and age. Someone 65 or over gets a bigger government rebate on their premium than someone under 65 on the same income. This rebate increases further for those aged 70 and over.

From April 2027, the government proposes removing that age-based bonus. So the rebate would be equal for everyone on the same income, regardless of age.

The government argues this fixes a subsidy that’s inequitable and poorly targeted, so will improve intergenerational equity.

Its own modelling predicts the vast majority of affected policyholders — about 99 per cent — would keep their cover. This means about 44,000 would drop it.

This agrees with our earlier research showing most older Australians don’t need a bigger rebate to keep their insurance.

But last week, Private Healthcare Australia released polling of more than 1,500 people showing 39 per cent of insured older Australians say they’d be more likely to drop their cover.

Based on the number of privately insured Australians aged 65 and over, that would mean about one million people, considerably more than the government’s predictions.

Our new research looks at the impacts of the government’s proposal. We used a decade of tax data, taking into account how the rebate had shifted over time.

What makes our research unique is that we separated out the impact of Australia’s two big private health insurance levers — the rebate and the Medicare Levy Surcharge tax penalty. That means we could focus on the impact of scrapping the extra health insurance rebates for the over 65s without muddying the waters.

We estimated 14,821–42,498 older Australians would drop their cover. The range depends on how we sampled the data and accounts for uncertainty in our modelling.

title.zh: 今年冬天什么时候去看全科医生、寻求紧急护理或去急诊室

summary.en: One state is asking people to consider their need to go to the emergency room this winter.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Getting the help you need for a winter illness could be simpler than spending hours waiting to be seen in a busy hospital emergency room.

That's the message the government is sending this flu season, a time when experts say hospitals tend to be the busiest, and wait times blow out.

While managing cold and flu cases is a national health concern, one state is taking a particularly strong stance, urging people to avoid the emergency room unless their lives are at risk.

On Monday, just under 10,000 people presented to emergency departments in Sydney, which the NSW health minister has described as the "biggest ever recorded winter day in history".

Professor Paul Griffin from the University of Queensland School of Medicine told SBS News that while numbers will vary between states, this time of year is often busy nationwide.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Across Australia, Griffin said healthcare services were seeing presentations of flu and RSV (respiratory syncytial virus), as well as an increase in COVID-19 cases.

While these can be concerning conditions, an emergency room will always prioritise the most severe health conditions first, Griffin explained.

"If you don't need to go to your emergency department, it does free up valuable resources for them to be able to deal with more emerging cases," he said.

"There are a number of viable options for people that have conditions that are a little bit less urgent, and that's why we want people to make sure that they understand where the best place for them to go really is."

The Australian government has outlined three broad categories of care — routine, urgent and emergency — each with varying symptom severity, encompassing flu symptoms as well as broader conditions.

Most health issues can be addressed through routine care, which for many people means their GP.

Griffin said GPs are not only a good touchpoint for receiving care when sick but can also help you prepare a plan ahead of potential illness.

They can provide health checks, vaccinations and offer family and individual health advice.

"If it's something that you're not feeling needs urgent attention, then your GP is often the best place to start to get the care that you need," Griffin said.

If you start experiencing symptoms like chest pain or feel like a respiratory illness is worsening, you may want to consider going to an urgent care clinic (UCC) or the hospital.

title.en: Kmart’s $89 glasses can record what you see. But what happens next?
title.zh: Kmart的89澳元眼镜能记录你所见。但接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Experts note a global surge in camera and smart glasses, but warn that regulating and enforcing rules for this wearable technology presents significant complexities.
summary.zh: 专家指出，全球范围内相机和智能眼镜等可穿戴技术正在迅速普及，但对其进行监管和执法却面临着更为复杂的挑战。

body.en:
Kmart recently launched a new accessory — dubbed Camera Glasses — which it said blends stylish eyewear with built-in camera technology.

At a glance, the black-framed spectacles from Kmart's in-house brand Anko look like any ordinary pair of glasses. But by Monday 3 August, there were reports the product was sold out online.

At $89, the glasses provide a low-cost alternative to the smart glasses designed by glasses company Ray-Ban and Facebook owners Meta, which start at $337. The latest generation of this technology costs more than $700.

A recent promotional video for Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, featuring celebrity Kylie Jenner, showcased its features. Those include an ultra-HD camera, discreet open-ear Bluetooth speakers, and translation technology.

In July, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said people who don't wear smart glasses in the future will be at a "pretty significant cognitive disadvantage".

There are similar products available or in development by the companies Samsung, Rokid, Even Realities, Solos and XREAL.

Milica Stilinovic is a postdoctoral research associate for the Governing Immersive Tech Project at the University of Sydney. She told SBS News that "a lot of flak has been driven towards Meta currently because they are market leaders".

But she said: "If the price is cheaper ... if you're not paying at the bridge, you may pay at the toll.

"We still need to ask ourselves, this data that we're essentially generating for these companies; how is it being handled, by whom and at what cost?"

Stilinovic also said wearable technology, regardless of its price point, raises complex questions around privacy and security.

Depending on the product, they may have AI-enabled programs embedded, which analyse human behaviours including eye movements, head tracking and voice patterns.

"They are picking up data of where you're walking around, the space that you're in, what you're doing at particular times ... even to the extent of knowing the map out of your home," Stilinovic said.

Facial recognition technology is not active in most smart glasses on the market.

However, in 2024, students from Harvard University combined smart glasses, facial search engines, AI language tools and public databases to test surveillance capabilities. They found information including a person's home address, name and phone number — just by looking at them.

Fareed Kaviani is a research fellow at the Emerging Technologies Research Lab at Monash University. In 2024, he co-authored a paper examining social perceptions of smart glasses use in Australia.

title.en: 'Not a lot of time for nerves': At a Greek airbase, this Australian is waiting for a call
title.zh: 澳大利亚人正在欧洲度过夏季，等待15分钟的火情警报

summary.en: Australian aerial firefighting pilots are increasingly spending their European summers assisting local authorities in combating wildfires, often waiting for short-notice deployment.
summary.zh: 越来越多的澳大利亚空中消防飞行员在欧洲夏季帮助当地政府扑灭野火，他们常常在等待短时间通知后立即投入工作。

body.en:
While most Australians in Europe are at the beach, NSW aerial firefighting pilot Alex Pay spends his long summer days at a Greek airbase, waiting for a call to action.

"When you get a fire call, you're gonna be airborne in 15 minutes," he told SBS News.

Once in the air, Pay can spend up to 10 hours supporting local authorities in Greece's fight against wildfires, which over the past week saw two pilots killed and hundreds of thousands forced to evacuate.

Pay, 31, works for a small but growing number of Australian private aerial firefighting companies based in Western Europe during this year's fire season, which is shaping up to be the continent's worst in record.

It also comes as Australia's own looming El Niño threatens to turn up the heat on our own summer bushfire risk .

Pay is a third-generation pilot with Pay's Air Service, which is based in the NSW Hunter Region.

"I remember as a kid flying with my dad to visit my grandparents," he told SBS News.

He pilots one of 14 aircraft his company has based throughout Greece for the summer. It’s his second season in the country, and the fifth overall for his company.

They fly a variant of the Air Tractor AT-802, nicknamed the "Fire Boss" — an amphibious aircraft that scoops water into a tank, or "hopper", controlled by a computerised fire gate that can be adjusted to match exact conditions.

In Australia, there were around 130 certified firefighting aeroplane operators or individual pilots, with a further 186 helicopter operators in 2021, according to Australia's Civil Aviation Authority.

Andrew Mackay is from Ballarat-based Field Air Group, which also has planes stationed in Greece this summer supporting Pay's.

"We like to say in our industry that it's not the aircraft that put out the fires, it's the ground crew — we're merely a tool to assist them," he told SBS News.

He said pilots will often work on either side of the fire to create a "triangle or an arrowhead, so the fire comes to a point where the ground crew can then extinguish that".

Sometimes they will drop water or retardant directly onto a house under threat from a blaze.

"We spent a lot of time training and preparing scenarios that give us a good education on what we might see on the fire ground," Pay said.

On Sunday, a Greek and a Danish national were killed after two helicopters collided while fighting a fire west of Athens.

The helicopters were leased from Australian company McDermott Aviation, which said in a statement it was "deeply saddened" by the tragedy.
